label: Activation not measurable from mutation calls
text: PITFALL: The claim is functional (mutations ACTIVATE the pathway), but this dataset has only mutations, SVs, panel and clinical tables; there are no expression, phospho-protein or RPPA data to measure pathway activation. CHECK: list all files in /biodsa-data and confirm whether any table measures MAPK/ERK activity (mRNA, protein, phospho, signature score). IF FOUND absent: the presence of ARAF N217I/G322S calls alone cannot show activation; lean toward 'Not verifiable' unless a defensible indirect test exists, and say why in the reasoning. SOURCE: general principle; no web source retrieved (search tool failed).

label: No WES variable in data
text: PITFALL: The hypothesis compares targeted-panel TMB with WES TMB, but this dataset (MSK-IMPACT panels IMPACT341/410/468 only, per data_gene_panel_matrix.txt) appears to contain no WES-derived TMB column or exome mutation calls. CHECK: grep all files for exome/WES columns; confirm whether any sample has two assays or any column is labelled WES/exome TMB. IF FOUND none: do not substitute panel-vs-panel or MUTATION_RATE-vs-TMB_NONSYNONYMOUS comparisons as proxies for WES; label Not verifiable unless a genuine WES measurement exists. SOURCE: library inspection of /biodsa-data headers (web search unavailable).

label: Exposure variable may be absent
text: PITFALL: The exposure (community-level average income, e.g. census-tract/zip median income) or a genetic-ancestry variable may simply not exist in the tables, and analysts substitute a proxy (race, smoking, PSA, disease extent) and then answer True/False. CHECK: grep every column header and the # description lines of data_clinical_patient.txt and data_clinical_sample.txt for income, SES, zip, census, tract, deprivation, ADI, ancestry, admixture; header scan by the library found only RACE (White/Black/Asian), no income or ancestry column. IF FOUND absent: the hypothesis cannot be tested; label Not verifiable rather than using a proxy. SOURCE: none (web search unavailable; task instructions).

label: No miRNA expression data present
text: PITFALL: The hypothesis concerns miRNA expression levels, but this study's files (clinical sample, CNA, seg, mutations, gene panel matrix) are DNA-level MSK-IMPACT targeted-panel data with no miRNA or mRNA expression file. CHECK: list /biodsa-data and confirm no data_mirna*/data_expression*/data_mrna* file exists; grep -i '^MIR' in data_cna.txt Hugo_Symbol column (library check found 0 MIR genes among ~416 rows). IF FOUND (no expression data): the hypothesis cannot be tested; label Not verifiable rather than True/False. SOURCE: https://docs.cbioportal.org/file-formats/ (unverified, search tool down).

label: Circular TMB-vs-TMB correlation
text: PITFALL: MUTATION_RATE and TMB_NONSYNONYMOUS in the clinical sample table are both derived from the same panel mutation calls (count divided by panel Mb), so correlating them, or correlating either with mutation counts from data_mutations.txt, is circular and is not a panel-vs-WES comparison. CHECK: recompute both from data_mutations.txt per sample and panel size; if they match up to scaling they are the same measurement. IF FOUND: do not report that correlation as evidence for or against the hypothesis. SOURCE: Chalmers et al. 2017 Genome Med, https://doi.org/10.1186/s13073-017-0424-2 (cited from memory, not retrieved).

label: No drug-response variable: likely Not verifiable
text: PITFALL: The hypothesis concerns chemotherapy response of tumoroids engrafted in mice, but these cBioPortal tables (patient sex; sample therapy-prior-to-derivation, site, MSI, TMB; mutations; CNA) appear to contain no engraftment, in vivo drug-response, IC50/AUC, tumour-volume or clinical-response variable. Inferring response from genomics or from prior-therapy text answers a different question. CHECK: grep every clinical column name and description for respon/sensitiv/IC50/AUC/volume/xenograft/mouse/engraft/RECIST/TRG; a first library grep found none. IF FOUND none: label Not verifiable rather than True/False. SOURCE: domain knowledge (web search unavailable).

label: Presence of mutation is not activation
text: PITFALL: Confirming that ARAF N217I and G322S are present in the mutation table is easily mistaken for supporting the hypothesis, but presence does not show functional effect. CHECK: grep data_mutations.txt for Hugo_Symbol==ARAF and HGVSp_Short p.N217I / p.G322S; record sample IDs, VAF (t_alt_count/t_depth if present) and Variant_Classification. IF FOUND: report them as observations that are consistent with the study's premise, and keep 'the mutation exists' separate from 'the mutation activates MAPK'. SOURCE: general principle; no web source retrieved.

label: Key: VTE/anticoagulation variables absent
text: PITFALL: The hypothesis needs three variables (VTE outcome, anticoagulation exposure, ctDNA status), and this dataset's clinical tables appear to have only SEX, RACE, ETHNICITY (patient) and CANCER_TYPE, CANCER_TYPE_DETAILED, ONCOTREE_CODE, TMB_NONSYNONYMOUS (sample), with no VTE, thrombosis, anticoagulant, treatment, follow-up or survival column. CHECK: grep every header and the '#' description lines of all six files for VTE/thrombo/embol/DVT/PE/anticoag/heparin/LMWH/DOAC/apixaban/rivaroxaban/warfarin/time/status. IF FOUND none: the outcome and the exposure are missing, so the claim cannot be tested and the right label is 'Not verifiable'. Do not swap in TMB or mutation counts as a proxy for VTE. SOURCE: direct inspection of /biodsa-data headers (library, no web source).

label: Race is not ancestry
text: PITFALL: Self-reported race is not genetic ancestry; ancestry is normally inferred from germline SNPs (e.g. MSK-IMPACT off-target reads), and race cannot stand in for both covariates. CHECK: look for an ancestry column (e.g. EUR/AFR/EAS fractions); none seen in the header scan. IF FOUND absent: note that the 'adjusting for ancestry' part is not doable; do not claim ancestry-adjusted results. SOURCE: none (web search unavailable).

label: Correlation vs agreement
text: PITFALL: Correlation (Pearson r) is not agreement; panel TMB can correlate highly with WES TMB yet be systematically biased (panels often overestimate, scaling differs by panel/pipeline). CHECK: if paired data existed, report Spearman/Pearson on log TMB plus Bland-Altman bias and limits of agreement, and the concordance at the 10 mut/Mb cutoff. IF FOUND: answer the correlation hypothesis with correlation, but do not over-interpret agreement. SOURCE: Bland & Altman 1986 Lancet; Merino et al. 2020 J Immunother Cancer (FoCR TMB harmonization), https://doi.org/10.1136/jitc-2019-000147 (cited from memory).

label: CNA is not an expression proxy
text: PITFALL: Using copy-number gain/amplification or mutations of a host gene as a proxy for miRNA upregulation; CNA does not reliably equal expression change, and GISTIC-style calls are relative to the tumour's matched normal, not an expression comparison vs normal liver. CHECK: whether any analysis step substitutes CNA/seg values for expression. IF FOUND: reject the proxy; absence of expression data means Not verifiable, not False. SOURCE: https://docs.cbioportal.org/file-formats/#discrete-copy-number-data (unverified).

label: Prior therapy is not response
text: PITFALL: THERAPY_PRIOR_TO_DERIVATION records patient treatment before the organoid was derived. It is not the organoid's or the mouse's response to chemotherapy, so it cannot show uniform or heterogeneous sensitivity in mice. CHECK: tabulate the column (about 287 of 340 samples are blank; the rest are FOLFOX/CRT/FOLFIRI/SCRT strings). IF FOUND: do not use it as a response outcome; at most it is an exposure covariate. SOURCE: domain knowledge (web search unavailable).

label: Mutual exclusivity underpowered
text: PITFALL: Mutual exclusivity with KRAS/BRAF/NRAS hotspots is indirect evidence of a MAPK driver role, but with roughly 8 WXS samples it has almost no statistical power, and over-reading it either way is an error. CHECK: count samples carrying KRAS G12/G13/Q61, BRAF V600 or NRAS hotspots and see whether they overlap with ARAF-mutant samples; run a Fisher test only to show how little power there is. IF FOUND: treat exclusivity as weak, suggestive evidence only; it can neither confirm nor refute activation. SOURCE: mutual exclusivity method literature (e.g. Ciriello et al. 2012 MEMo, Genome Res); not retrieved.

label: ctDNA status derivable but insufficient
text: PITFALL: The gene panel is ACCESS129 (MSK-ACCESS, a plasma cfDNA panel), so ctDNA+/- status could be derived from whether a sample has somatic mutation calls. Being able to build the ctDNA grouping does not make the hypothesis testable without VTE and anticoagulation data. CHECK: confirm the panel IDs in data_gene_panel_matrix.txt and that TMB_NONSYNONYMOUS=0 for many samples (about 2229 of 5570). IF FOUND: treat this as only 1 of the 3 required variables, and don't call the hypothesis True/False from ctDNA-vs-cancer-type or ctDNA-vs-TMB comparisons. SOURCE: direct inspection of data files (no web source).

label: Panel size heterogeneity
text: PITFALL: Panel TMB precision depends on panel size (IMPACT341 ~0.98 Mb, 410 ~1.06 Mb, 468 ~1.22 Mb); small panels give noisy TMB at low values and mixing panels without normalising by covered Mb biases comparisons. CHECK: tabulate GENE_PANEL per sample and confirm TMB is divided by the correct panel size. IF FOUND mixing: stratify by panel or normalise per Mb. SOURCE: Buchhalter et al. 2019 Int J Cancer, https://doi.org/10.1002/ijc.31878; Chalmers 2017 (cited from memory).

label: 8q arm calls and duplicates
text: PITFALL: 8q status in data_clinical_sample.txt column 8Q_ARM has Gain/Neutral/Loss and 'Not called' (about 120 samples); treating Not called as Neutral biases estimates, and patients can have several samples. CHECK: count values and samples per patient. IF FOUND: drop Not called, keep one sample per patient (e.g. first or primary), and model sample type (primary vs metastatic) as a covariate because 8q gain is enriched in metastases. SOURCE: none (web search unavailable).

label: No normal liver comparator
text: PITFALL: The hypothesis requires a normal-liver comparison group, but all 19 samples are SAMPLE_CLASS=Tumor (10 HCC, 9 LIAD/hepatocellular adenoma); matched normals (_N barcodes in mutations) were used only for somatic calling and have no profiled values. CHECK: tabulate SAMPLE_CLASS and ONCOTREE_CODE in data_clinical_sample.txt; look for any normal-tissue columns in data files. IF FOUND (no normal group): a 'vs normal liver' contrast cannot be computed; label Not verifiable. SOURCE: https://www.cbioportal.org/ (unverified).

label: SCLC subtypes need expression data
text: PITFALL: SCLC subtypes (SCLC-A/N/P, ±Y/I) are defined by mRNA or protein (IHC) expression of ASCL1, NEUROD1, POU2F3, YAP1, not by DNA mutations or copy number; this dataset has no expression table (only mutations, CNA, seg, SV, clinical). CHECK: list files and grep all columns/headers for expression, RNA, IHC, or subtype labels (none found: no ASCL1/NEUROD1/POU2F3 in clinical, mutation or SV files). IF FOUND absent: the relevant variable does not exist, which points to Not verifiable rather than True/False. SOURCE: Rudin et al. 2019 Nat Rev Cancer, https://doi.org/10.1038/s41568-019-0133-9 (prior knowledge; web search failed).

label: Do not answer from priors
text: PITFALL: Published literature (Chalmers 2017; FoCR harmonization) reports strong panel-vs-WES TMB correlation, so an analyst may be tempted to answer False from prior knowledge rather than from the data. CHECK: confirm the answer rests on variables actually present in /biodsa-data. IF the data lack WES: the task's own definition says Not verifiable; prior literature is not data evidence. SOURCE: task instructions; Chalmers et al. 2017 https://doi.org/10.1186/s13073-017-0424-2.

label: ARAF variant position / prior knowledge
text: PITFALL: Known activating ARAF mutations sit mainly in the N-terminal regulatory region (S214, around P216/N217), which is homologous to the RAF1 S259 14-3-3 site; G322 is outside that region, so the two variants may have different functional evidence. CHECK: note the position of each variant relative to the CR2 regulatory region (around aa 214-217) and the kinase domain. IF FOUND: do not assume both variants behave the same; any argument by analogy (e.g. that N217 resembles S214) is prior knowledge, not evidence from this data. SOURCE: Imielinski et al. 2014 JCI (ARAF S214 in lung adenocarcinoma); not retrieved.

label: Sample suffix meaning pt/tm/IMPACT
text: PITFALL: Sample suffixes encode different material: -pt is the patient tumour and -tm the tumoroid/organoid (Sample Type Unknown_Tumor, Fresh); IM3/IM5/IM6 are clinical MSK-IMPACT panels of patient tumours. Matched pt/tm genomic concordance shows the organoid represents the tumour; it does not show drug-response uniformity. CHECK: count suffixes (about 21 pt, 31 tm, 287 IMPACT) and check for any mouse/xenograft sample class. IF FOUND only pt/tm pairs: do not treat genomic concordance or heterogeneity as evidence for or against the response claim. SOURCE: domain knowledge (web search unavailable).

label: ctDNA calling: CHIP confounding
text: PITFALL: If ctDNA status is derived, TMB=0 or no mutation rows does not equal ctDNA-negative. CHIP (clonal hematopoiesis) variants and germline calls can make a sample look ctDNA+, and failed or low-coverage samples can look ctDNA-. CHECK: look for CHIP genes (DNMT3A, TET2, ASXL1, PPM1D) and for whether matched-normal/WBC filtering is noted. IF FOUND: exclude CHIP genes when defining ctDNA+ and report how sensitive the result is to that choice. SOURCE: general cfDNA methodology (search tool unavailable; not retrieved).

label: Area-level income confounding
text: PITFALL: Even when area-level income exists, it is an ecological measure (ecological fallacy) and is confounded by race, disease stage, sample type and referral pattern at a tertiary centre. CHECK: whether income is per patient or aggregated; how much is missing. IF FOUND: use logistic regression of 8q gain on income plus race, ancestry, sample type and disease extent, and report the adjusted estimate and CI, not the crude association. SOURCE: none (web search unavailable).

label: Absence is not contradiction
text: PITFALL: Treating 'not verifiable' as 'False' — absence of evidence for miRNA upregulation in DNA panel data is not evidence against it. CHECK: before choosing False, confirm you actually measured the miRNAs (miR-452, miR-766, miR-1180) in HCA, HCC and normal liver and found no/opposite difference. IF FOUND (variables absent): use Not verifiable. SOURCE: task label definitions.

label: Somatic call QC on ARAF variants
text: PITFALL: Low-VAF or recurrent identical calls across samples may be artefacts or germline variants (dbSNP rs IDs appear in this MAF), not somatic drivers. CHECK: for the ARAF rows, check dbSNP_RS, the allele counts/VAF and whether the same coordinate recurs suspiciously; ARAF is on chrX, so adjust VAF expectations by sex. IF FOUND: a germline or artefact call weakens any driver interpretation. SOURCE: standard somatic variant QC practice; not retrieved.

label: Not-on-panel is not absent
text: PITFALL: Absence of a gene from CNA/mutation calls is not evidence the subtype is absent; ASCL1, NEUROD1 and POU2F3 appear not to be on MSK-IMPACT panels (no rows for them in data_cna.txt; YAP1 is present but all 0). CHECK: grep -E '^(ASCL1|NEUROD1|POU2F3)\b' data_cna.txt and gene_panel content. IF FOUND missing: treat as not measured (NA), never as 'not present'; do not infer subtype absence from missing rows. SOURCE: MSK-IMPACT panel description, Cheng et al. 2015 J Mol Diagn https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jmoldx.2014.12.006 (prior knowledge).

label: Genomic heterogeneity is not response heterogeneity
text: PITFALL: Genomic heterogeneity across tumoroids (varied KRAS/TP53/APC status, MSI, TMB) is sometimes taken as proof of heterogeneous drug response. Predicting chemosensitivity from mutations is weak and unvalidated for 5-FU/oxaliplatin/irinotecan in rectal cancer. CHECK: confirm whether any measured response variable exists before linking mutations to sensitivity. IF FOUND none: do not use genomic heterogeneity to reject 'uniform sensitivity'; label Not verifiable. SOURCE: domain knowledge (web search unavailable).

label: If outcome existed: confounding/competing risk
text: PITFALL: If VTE outcome data existed, a naive comparison of VTE rates in anticoagulated vs non-anticoagulated patients would suffer confounding by indication (anticoagulated patients have prior VTE or higher risk), immortal time bias, and death as a competing risk. CHECK: is anticoagulation timing relative to blood draw recorded, and is death recorded? IF FOUND: use landmark or time-varying exposure with Fine-Gray or cumulative-incidence (Aalen-Johansen) estimates, and test the anticoagulation x ctDNA interaction rather than comparing p-values between subgroups. SOURCE: standard cancer-associated thrombosis epidemiology (search unavailable).

label: Power and null results
text: PITFALL: Small minority groups (Black n=165, Asian n=63 of about 2069 patients) give low power, and a null adjusted result is not evidence against an association. CHECK: CI width for the income coefficient. IF FOUND wide CI: interpret cautiously; but this only matters if an income variable exists. SOURCE: none (web search unavailable).

label: miRNA DE stats if data existed
text: PITFALL (if expression data were present): miRNA DE with tiny groups (9 HCA, 10 HCC) and three miRNAs tested in two contrasts needs multiple-testing correction and appropriate normalisation (e.g. limma/edgeR/DESeq2 or delta-Ct with stable reference); low-abundance miRNAs like miR-1180 are prone to dropout. CHECK: group sizes, normalisation, FDR across 6 tests, and that 'both HCA and HCC' requires each contrast significant. IF FOUND: apply BH-FDR and require significance in both contrasts. SOURCE: https://bioconductor.org/packages/limma (unverified).

label: DNA proxies for subtype unreliable
text: PITFALL: Using DNA proxies (e.g., MYC amplification, RB1/TP53 status, YAP1 CNA, NOTCH mutations) to assign SCLC subtype is unreliable; associations (e.g., MYC with NEUROD1/POU2F3-high) are only enrichments. CHECK: whether any proxy claim is backed by an expression variable in the data. IF FOUND only DNA proxies: do not label True/False from proxies; at most mention as weak context. SOURCE: Rudin et al. 2019 Nat Rev Cancer https://doi.org/10.1038/s41568-019-0133-9; Mollaoglu et al. 2017 Cancer Cell (prior knowledge).

label: Absence of evidence is not False
text: PITFALL: Labelling the hypothesis 'False' needs evidence against activation (e.g. measured low ERK activity in ARAF mutants); a lack of supporting data is not contradiction. CHECK: ask whether any variable in the data could show that the pathway is NOT activated in ARAF-mutant tumours. IF FOUND absent: choose between True and Not verifiable, not False. SOURCE: task label definitions.

label: Gene panel coverage differs
text: PITFALL: Mixing gene panels (IMPACT341/410/468/505) makes TMB and gene-level mutation/CNA calls incomparable across samples, because genes absent from a panel look wild-type. CHECK: use data_gene_panel_matrix.txt to restrict each comparison to genes covered by all panels involved, and normalise TMB per Mb. IF FOUND: restrict to shared genes, or stratify by panel. SOURCE: domain knowledge (web search unavailable).

label: Multiple samples per patient
text: PITFALL: If one patient has several samples (e.g. T02, T03 suffixes), counting samples instead of patients inflates n and mixes timepoints. CHECK: compare unique PATIENT_ID vs SAMPLE_ID counts in data_clinical_sample.txt. IF FOUND: collapse to one sample per patient (e.g. first or baseline draw) before any patient-level analysis. SOURCE: general practice (no web source).

label: Literature vs data availability
text: PITFALL: Prior literature shows PDX/CDX SCLC models do recapitulate ASCL1-, NEUROD1- and POU2F3-high subtypes, so the hypothesis is biologically implausible — but outside knowledge must not substitute for data analysis when the dataset lacks the variable. CHECK: confirm whether the dataset itself contains subtype/expression variables before choosing False. IF FOUND none: answer from the data's content (Not verifiable), noting literature only as context. SOURCE: Drapkin et al. 2018 Cancer Discov https://doi.org/10.1158/2159-8290.CD-17-0935; Huang et al. 2018 Genes Dev (POU2F3) (prior knowledge).

label: Do not import published results
text: PITFALL: In this kind of study, cBioPortal holds only genomics; the in vivo chemo-response results (e.g. tumour volume in mice) sit in the paper's supplementary data, which the teams do not have. A team may wrongly fill in 'known' published findings. CHECK: base the label only on variables present in the provided files. IF FOUND none: Not verifiable; do not import external knowledge of the study's results. SOURCE: task instructions / domain knowledge.

label: Sample class is not subtype
text: PITFALL: data_clinical_sample.txt has SAMPLE_CLASS (42 PDX, 27 Tumor) but no CDX label and no subtype column; teams may conflate PDX sample class with subtype evidence. CHECK: tabulate SAMPLE_CLASS, CANCER_TYPE_DETAILED, ONCOTREE_CODE; look for any column naming ASCL1/NEUROD1/POU2F3/subtype. IF FOUND none: the presence of PDX models alone says nothing about which transcriptional subtypes they carry. SOURCE: cBioPortal clinical data format docs https://docs.cbioportal.org/file-formats/ (prior knowledge).

label: WXS misses TERT promoter
text: PITFALL: The mutation file comes from whole-exome sequencing (gene panel matrix says WXS), and exome capture usually misses the TERT promoter hotspots C228T/C250T (hg19 chr5:1,295,228 and 1,295,250; on the minus strand they show as G>A), so a missing call does not mean wild type. CHECK: grep TERT in data_mutations.txt; look at Variant_Classification (5'Flank/Promoter/5'UTR) and Start_Position near 1295228/1295250; also grep every clinical column header for TERT. IF FOUND none: there is no promoter-mutation variable, and the honest label leans Not verifiable; do not call untested samples wild type. SOURCE: domain knowledge (Killela 2013 PNAS doi:10.1073/pnas.1303607110; Barthel 2017 Nat Genet doi:10.1038/ng.3823); web search was unavailable.

label: No proxies for TERTp
text: PITFALL: TERT coding or missense mutations, TERT copy-number gain (data_cna) or TERT expression itself are not stand-ins for TERT promoter mutation status. CHECK: confirm that any TERT variant used really is at the -124/-146 promoter hotspots, not in the coding sequence. IF FOUND only coding mutations or CNA: do not relabel them as promoter mutations; report that the promoter variable is missing. SOURCE: domain knowledge (Huang 2013 Science doi:10.1126/science.1229259); web search unavailable.

label: IDH/ATRX confounding
text: PITFALL: IDH-mutant/G-CIMP gliomas rarely carry TERT promoter mutations and often use ATRX/ALT instead, with low TERT, so a crude comparison mixes up IDH status with TERTp. CHECK: tabulate TERTp status against IDH1_MUTATION and G_CIMP_METHYLATION in data_clinical_sample.txt, and ATRX mutations. IF FOUND imbalance: also test within IDH-wild-type samples only (or adjust for IDH) and report both results. SOURCE: domain knowledge (Killela 2013 PNAS; Arita 2013 Acta Neuropathol doi:10.1007/s00401-013-1109-7); web search unavailable.

label: Low TERT expression handling
text: PITFALL: TERT mRNA is low in RNA-seq (many RSEM values near 0), so a t-test on raw values or on z-scores with outliers can mislead. CHECK: count zeros and look at the distribution of TERT in data_mrna_seq_v2_rsem.txt. IF FOUND skewed or zero-inflated: use log2(RSEM+1) with a Mann-Whitney test, report group medians, effect size and the fraction expressing TERT, and use one expression file consistently. SOURCE: domain knowledge (Barthel 2017 Nat Genet); web search unavailable.

label: Absence of evidence
text: PITFALL: The hypothesis is a negative claim (no correlation), and a non-significant test in a small or underpowered group does not support it; the published consensus is that TERTp-mutant tumours have higher TERT mRNA. CHECK: report the n per group, the effect size and its confidence interval, not just the p-value. IF FOUND small n or a wide CI: do not answer True just because p>0.05; a clear expression rise in mutants means False. SOURCE: domain knowledge (Killela 2013; Barthel 2017); web search unavailable.

label: Sample ID matching
text: PITFALL: Sample IDs may differ between files (TCGA barcodes of 12, 15 or longer characters, recurrent samples, duplicate aliquots), which drops or mismatches samples. CHECK: map the mutation Tumor_Sample_Barcode and the expression column names to the 15-character SAMPLE_ID; count the overlap; keep primary tumours only (SAMPLE_TYPE). IF FOUND mismatch: truncate the barcodes consistently and remove duplicates before testing. SOURCE: domain knowledge (TCGA barcode conventions, docs.gdc.cancer.gov); web search unavailable.

label: Compare head-to-head, not just significance
text: PITFALL: Showing the genetic model (sample column PROGNOSTIC_MODEL, Low/Medium/High risk) is merely significant in Cox/log-rank does not show it OUTPERFORMS established methods. CHECK: Fit Cox OS models on the same complete-case patients for IPI (patient IPI column) alone, PROGNOSTIC_MODEL alone, and both; compare Harrell C-index (with bootstrap CI of the difference), AIC, and likelihood-ratio test of PROGNOSTIC_MODEL added to IPI. IF FOUND: Support the hypothesis only if the genetic model has higher C-index than IPI and adds significant information beyond IPI; otherwise lean False. SOURCE: Harrell, Regression Modeling Strategies (2015); Steyerberg, Clinical Prediction Models (2019) [not retrieved: search tool down].

label: Optimism of in-sample model
text: PITFALL: The genetic risk model was likely derived (trained) in this same cohort, so its apparent discrimination is optimistically biased versus IPI, which was externally defined. CHECK: Read the data_clinical_sample.txt column descriptions for PROGNOSTIC_MODEL; check whether all/most samples have it (training) or a subset (validation). IF FOUND: Treat an in-sample C-index advantage as weak evidence; note optimism; if only a small margin, do not call it outperforming without caveat. SOURCE: Steyerberg et al., J Clin Epidemiol 2001;54:774 (internal validation) [not retrieved].

label: Same-patient comparison set
text: PITFALL: Missing IPI and missing PROGNOSTIC_MODEL differ across patients (e.g. DLBCL_DUKE_658 has blank IPI); comparing C-indices on different subsets is invalid because C-index depends on case mix and follow-up. CHECK: Count non-missing OS_MONTHS, OS_STATUS, IPI, PROGNOSTIC_MODEL; restrict all compared models to the identical intersection. IF FOUND: Report N used; if the intersection is small, widen CIs and be cautious. SOURCE: Harrell, Regression Modeling Strategies [not retrieved].

label: Survival coding in cBioPortal files
text: PITFALL: OS_STATUS is coded as strings like '0:LIVING'/'1:DECEASED' and OS_MONTHS may contain blanks or zeros; mis-parsing flips the event indicator and reverses concordance. CHECK: Parse the integer before the colon as the event; drop missing/negative times; confirm high-risk groups have more events as a sanity check. IF FOUND: Fix coding before any Cox model. SOURCE: cBioPortal file format documentation, docs.cbioportal.org/file-formats [not retrieved].

label: Fair coding of comparator
text: PITFALL: Comparing a 3-level categorical model (Low/Medium/High) against IPI used as a continuous 0-5 score or as grouped categories gives different C-indices; cell-of-origin (ABC/GCB) is another established method but may be absent from the tables. CHECK: Evaluate IPI both as 0-5 score and as standard groups (0-1 low, 2 low-int, 3 high-int, 4-5 high), and look for any COO column; the genetic model should beat IPI in a fair coding. IF FOUND: Report both codings; if the conclusion depends on coding, say so. SOURCE: International NHL Prognostic Factors Project, NEJM 1993;329:987 [not retrieved].

label: Censoring bias in C-index
text: PITFALL: Harrell's C-index is biased by heavy censoring and long follow-up tails; with differing censoring patterns comparisons can mislead. CHECK: Check censoring fraction and median follow-up; compute Uno's C or time-dependent AUC at e.g. 3 and 5 years as a sensitivity analysis. IF FOUND: Prefer truncated/Uno C (survival::concordance with timewt='n/G2' or ymax) for the comparison. SOURCE: Uno et al., Stat Med 2011;30:1105 [not retrieved].

label: Independence beyond IPI
text: PITFALL: A univariable significant genetic model may lose significance after adjusting for IPI, meaning it partly re-encodes clinical risk. CHECK: Multivariable Cox with PROGNOSTIC_MODEL + IPI (or IPI factors); check PH assumption with cox.zph/Schoenfeld residuals. IF FOUND: If PROGNOSTIC_MODEL is independent and stronger (bigger HR, LRT), supports True; if not independent, supports False. SOURCE: Grambsch & Therneau, Biometrika 1994;81:515 [not retrieved].

label: Promoter variants hide in non-coding classes
text: PITFALL: In MAF files, promoter mutations are not coding: they show up as Variant_Classification 5'Flank (or sometimes IGR or 5'UTR) and Consequence upstream_gene_variant, so filtering to nonsynonymous classes or relying on HGVSp hides them all. CHECK: grep every NFKBIE row in data_mutations.txt (Hugo_Symbol and the SYMBOL/all_effects columns) and tabulate Variant_Classification, Consequence and Start_Position. IF FOUND: count 5'Flank/upstream/5'UTR rows near the NFKBIE TSS as candidate promoter mutations, and do not drop non-coding classes. SOURCE: https://docs.gdc.cancer.gov/Data/File_Formats/MAF_Format/ (not retrieved; search tool down)

label: Focal amplification data absent
text: PITFALL: The hypothesis is compound (KIT mutations AND focal amplifications), but the dataset has no copy-number table (no data_cna / segment / GISTIC file; only clinical, gene panel, mutations, mutsig). CHECK: ls /biodsa-data and confirm no CNA/segment file; note data_mutations.txt has a Tumorscape_Amplification_Peaks column, which is a gene-level annotation of pan-cancer amplification peaks, NOT a per-sample amplification call. IF FOUND: do not use the Tumorscape/TCGAscape annotation columns or ABSOLUTE ploidy as a proxy for focal amplification; treat the amplification half as untestable and weigh whether the claim can be judged on the KIT-mutation half alone (and say so explicitly in reasoning). SOURCE: domain knowledge (web search tool returned HTTP 403; unverified).

label: NFKBIE is on minus strand; check coordinates
text: PITFALL: NFKBIE (chr6p21.1, GRCh37 about chr6:44,225,000-44,233,000) lies on the minus strand, so its promoter sits at the higher-coordinate end, just past the gene end. Analysts often look below the start coordinate and miss it. CHECK: list every chr6 variant within about 2 kb of the NFKBIE TSS (the highest coordinate of the canonical transcript ENST00000275015) in the GRCh37 build shown in NCBI_Build, whatever Hugo_Symbol says, since flank variants may be assigned to a neighbouring gene. IF FOUND: treat them as promoter mutations, and note recurrent positions and whether they look like C>T/CC>TT UV-type changes. SOURCE: https://grch37.ensembl.org/Homo_sapiens/Gene/Summary?g=NFKBIE (not retrieved)

label: CALR mutations are indels
text: PITFALL: CALR driver mutations in MPN are exon 9 frameshift indels (type 1 = 52-bp deletion, type 2 = 5-bp insertion, plus other rarer indels), so keeping only SNVs or missense/nonsense rows hides them all. CHECK: select Hugo_Symbol == 'CALR' with every Variant_Classification, including Frame_Shift_Del, Frame_Shift_Ins and In_Frame_*, and look at HGVSp/Protein Change and DNA Change. IF FOUND: count indel rows as CALR mutations; never filter by Variant_Type == SNP. SOURCE: domain knowledge (web search unavailable, HTTP 403).

label: Dataset has no ccRCC samples
text: PITFALL: The dataset may not contain the tumour type named in the hypothesis; header inspection shows data_clinical_sample.txt CANCER_TYPE/ONCOTREE_CODE values are colorectal (COAD, READ, COADREAD), small bowel (SBC, SIC, DA) and CUP, with IBD-related columns, and no RCC/CCRCC/kidney samples. CHECK: tabulate CANCER_TYPE, CANCER_TYPE_DETAILED, ONCOTREE_CODE and PRIMARY_SITE and grep all files for 'renal|kidney|RCC|CCRCC'. IF FOUND (no ccRCC): the hypothesis about ccRCC cannot be tested with these data; do not substitute colorectal tumours, and the label should be 'Not verifiable'. SOURCE: direct inspection of /biodsa-data headers (research tool unavailable).

label: Use published subtype labels
text: PITFALL: Subtype labels come from clinical MUTATION_TYPE (BRAF_Hotspot_Mutants 150, RAS_Hotspot_Mutants 92, NF1_Any_Mutants 28, Triple_WT 46, NA 43); recomputing subtypes from the MAF or including NA samples changes group sizes. CHECK: use data_clinical_sample MUTATION_TYPE as the grouping; exclude NA rather than lumping into non-Triple-WT, and run a sensitivity analysis with NA included in the comparator. IF FOUND: report both; prefer the published labels as primary. SOURCE: domain knowledge (search unavailable).

label: Restrict to desmoplastic samples
text: PITFALL: The cohort may mix desmoplastic and other melanomas, or pure and mixed desmoplastic histology, so counting mutations across the whole MAF can mislabel the result. CHECK: join Tumor_Sample_Barcode to SAMPLE_ID and keep ONCOTREE_CODE=DESM / CANCER_TYPE_DETAILED 'Desmoplastic Melanoma'. Report counts by DETAILED_SAMPLE_HISTOLOGY_CATEGORY (Pure vs Mixed). IF FOUND: the hypothesis is about desmoplastic melanoma, so one or more NFKBIE promoter mutations in DESM samples contradicts 'absent'. SOURCE: https://docs.cbioportal.org/file-formats/ (not retrieved)

label: Defining JAK2-nonmutated
text: PITFALL: Deciding JAK2-nonmutated status only from JAK2 rows in the MAF can misclassify patients. Exon 12 JAK2 mutations count as well as V617F, and the MAF has a per-sample column 'JAK2/MPL mutation' with values JAK2, MPL or unmutated. CHECK: cross-tabulate the 'JAK2/MPL mutation' column against whether each sample has any JAK2 row, and against whether it has any CALR row. IF FOUND (disagreement): define JAK2-nonmutated as no JAK2 mutation by either source, and report both definitions. SOURCE: domain knowledge (web search unavailable).

label: ITH needs multi-region sampling
text: PITFALL: Showing ITH in ALL tumours of a type needs several spatially separate samples per tumour (multi-region sequencing, e.g. Gerlinger 2012 NEJM / TRACERx Renal); a single biopsy per tumour misses ITH and cannot show that ITH is present in every case. CHECK: count samples per PATIENT_ID and check whether repeated samples come from the same primary tumour region (not metastasis vs primary, not different panels); here only 4 of 175 patients have more than one sample. IF FOUND: there is no multi-region design, so universal-ITH claims cannot be tested; at most report descriptive subclonality, and label the claim not verifiable. SOURCE: Gerlinger et al. NEJM 2012 doi:10.1056/NEJMoa1113205 (not retrieved; tool down).

label: Filter KIT to nonsilent/driver
text: PITFALL: Counting all KIT variants (silent, intronic, UTR, passenger missense in hypermutated UV tumours) inflates KIT mutation rates in BRAF/RAS/NF1 groups and dilutes Triple-WT enrichment. CHECK: filter MAF to nonsynonymous classes (Missense, Nonsense, Frame_Shift, In_Frame, Splice_Site) and separately to known hotspot/driver KIT exons 9/11/13/17 (e.g. L576P, K642E, D816, V560). IF FOUND: base the test on per-sample presence of nonsilent (and ideally driver) KIT mutation, one count per sample, and report both all-nonsilent and hotspot-only results. SOURCE: domain knowledge (search unavailable).

label: No read counts in MAF
text: PITFALL: data_mutations.txt has empty t_ref_count/t_alt_count (all 18689 rows checked), so VAF/cellular-prevalence clustering (PyClone-style) cannot be run directly; analysts may wrongly conclude Not verifiable. CHECK: confirm read-count columns are empty; then test whether mutation presence/absence and copy-number segments differ between tumour (T) and xenograft (X) samples of the same patient. IF FOUND: use presence/absence of SNVs and CNA segment changes (gains/losses appearing or vanishing between T and X0/X1) as evidence of clonal shifts instead of VAF. SOURCE: domain knowledge (search tool failed); PyClone https://www.nature.com/articles/nmeth.2883

label: Absence claim: one hit falsifies; zero needs coverage
text: PITFALL: 'Absent' is a universal claim. A single confirmed somatic NFKBIE promoter mutation in a DESM sample makes it False. Zero hits only means True if the promoter was actually sequenced. CHECK: count DESM samples with NFKBIE promoter variants. If there are none, check whether the MAF has any 5'Flank/upstream/IGR rows at all, and which samples are whole-genome (GENE_PANEL 'Whole Genome') versus exome-only. IF FOUND: no non-coding calls at all means the promoter wasn't assayed, so the answer leans Not verifiable rather than True. Hits in DESM samples mean False. SOURCE: https://docs.gdc.cancer.gov/Data/File_Formats/MAF_Format/ (not retrieved)

label: JAK2-nonmutated includes MPL
text: PITFALL: 'JAK2-nonmutated' covers MPL-mutated patients as well as triple-negative ones. Restricting to 'unmutated' only narrows the group and could miss CALR carriers. CHECK: count CALR-mutated samples among JAK2/MPL status MPL, among unmutated, and among JAK2. IF FOUND: assess the hypothesis on all non-JAK2 samples (MPL + unmutated). CALR is usually mutually exclusive with JAK2 and MPL, so expect it mostly in the 'unmutated' group. SOURCE: domain knowledge (web search unavailable).

label: Panel VAF not enough for clonality
text: PITFALL: Inferring subclonality from the VAFs of one targeted-panel sample (MSK-IMPACT ~341-468 genes, FoundationOne 317 genes) is unreliable: few mutations, purity and copy-number confounding, and coverage limits. CHECK: count mutations per sample (often <10), check that TUMOR_PURITY and allele-specific CN are available, and note Foundation rows with no read counts. IF FOUND: do not call samples clonal or subclonal from raw VAF; a purity-and-CN-adjusted cancer cell fraction (e.g. PyClone/ABSOLUTE) is needed, and it is not feasible with this panel data. SOURCE: Roth et al. Nat Methods 2014 PyClone; Carter et al. Nat Biotech 2012 ABSOLUTE (not retrieved).

label: TMB confounding for KIT
text: PITFALL: Mutation burden confounding: NF1 and BRAF/RAS tumours are UV-hypermutated, so random passenger KIT hits are more likely there; Triple-WT have lower TMB, so raw rate comparisons can mislead either way. CHECK: compare TMB_NONSYNONYMOUS across subtypes; check KIT variant hotspot status per group. IF FOUND: emphasise hotspot/driver KIT mutations or adjust (logistic regression with log TMB). SOURCE: domain knowledge (search unavailable).

label: Parse passage from sample ID
text: PITFALL: Sample naming encodes lineage: SAxxxT = patient tumour, X0/X1 = first engraftment passage, X2..X6 = later serial passages, letters A-G = parallel/sibling xenografts. Mixing later passages with first engraftment confuses initial engraftment selection with later serial-passage drift. CHECK: parse SAMPLE_ID into patient, passage number, branch letter; identify which patients have both T and X0/X1. IF FOUND: compare T vs earliest passage (X0/X1) for the engraftment claim; treat later passages separately. SOURCE: domain knowledge (search tool failed)

label: Exome capture poorly covers promoters
text: PITFALL: Exome capture covers promoters only patchily (through off-target reads and UTR baits), so exome-only samples can look like they lack promoter mutations because of coverage, not biology. CHECK: use GENE_PANEL/PLATFORM to split samples into WGS and exome-only, and look at t_depth/t_alt_count for any promoter calls. IF FOUND: base claims of absence only on samples with WGS or demonstrated coverage, and state that limitation. SOURCE: https://www.nature.com/articles/nature14971 (not retrieved; TERT promoter detection relies on WGS or targeted assays)

label: Universal-negative claim logic
text: PITFALL: The hypothesis is a universal negative ('not present in any'). Using significance tests or proportions instead of a count gets the logic wrong. CHECK: count distinct patients who carry a somatic CALR mutation and have no JAK2 mutation. IF FOUND: if the count is 1 or more, the data contradict the claim (False). It is True only if CALR is assessable and the count is 0. It is Not verifiable only if CALR or JAK2 status truly cannot be determined. SOURCE: logic of the claim (web search unavailable).

label: Cross-panel/site discordance not ITH
text: PITFALL: Primary-vs-metastasis or multi-timepoint pairs show temporal/metastatic divergence, not intratumour heterogeneity, and different panels (IMPACT341/410/468 vs FoundationOne) create spurious private mutations. CHECK: for patients with more than one sample, compare SAMPLE_TYPE, GENE_PANEL and the panel gene overlap before calling discordant mutations. IF FOUND: restrict comparisons to the genes both panels cover; do not interpret differences between panels or between sites as ITH. SOURCE: general multi-sample sequencing practice (not retrieved).

label: Barcode matching
text: PITFALL: Sample-ID mismatches between MAF Tumor_Sample_Barcode and clinical SAMPLE_ID (e.g. -01 vs -06 suffix, metastatic samples, multiple samples per patient) silently drop or duplicate samples. CHECK: match barcodes to SAMPLE_ID and count matched samples per subtype; deduplicate to one sample per patient. IF FOUND: harmonise IDs (truncate to 15 chars) before computing per-sample KIT status. SOURCE: domain knowledge (search unavailable).

label: Match assay type T vs X
text: PITFALL: Comparing targeted-panel calls with whole-genome calls (or vice versa) creates false 'lost/gained' mutations driven by assay coverage, not clonal selection. CHECK: compare T vs X only within the same SEQUENCING_TYPE (-targeted vs -whole_genome suffix) and only at positions covered by both. IF FOUND: restrict comparisons to matched assay type; for targeted data, restrict to the shared panel sites. SOURCE: domain knowledge (search tool failed)

label: Germline and low-VAF artefacts
text: PITFALL: Non-coding calls are enriched for germline SNPs and low-support artefacts. CHECK: for NFKBIE promoter rows, inspect dbSNP_RS, GMAF/ExAC_AF, Mutation_Status, FILTER and t_alt_count/t_depth (VAF). IF FOUND: exclude common germline polymorphisms (population AF >1%) and calls with weak support. Report recurrent hotspot positions across samples as strong evidence of real somatic events. SOURCE: https://docs.gdc.cancer.gov/Data/File_Formats/MAF_Format/ (not retrieved)

label: Somatic vs germline CALR
text: PITFALL: Mutation rows may contain germline or low-level calls, and the claim is about somatic CALR. CHECK: for CALR rows, inspect 'Germline allele percentage (%)', 'Germline reads', 'Tumor allele burden (%)' and Mutation_Status. SOMATIC_STATUS in the clinical table says 'Matched' (tumour/normal). IF FOUND: exclude rows with substantial germline allele fraction. Treat matched-normal-filtered calls as somatic. SOURCE: domain knowledge (web search unavailable).

label: Universal claim needs proper design
text: PITFALL: A universal claim ('ITH in all tumours') can be rejected by one convincing counterexample only if it was properly sampled; a single-sample tumour that looks homogeneous is not a counterexample. CHECK: before labelling False, confirm that the relevant tumour type is present and was sampled across several regions. IF FOUND (absent): use 'Not verifiable', not 'False'. SOURCE: study-design reasoning.

label: Use Fisher exact test
text: PITFALL: Small counts (Triple-WT n=46, KIT mutants probably few) make chi-square invalid and 'enrichment' claims fragile. CHECK: build 2x2 table Triple-WT vs other (BRAF+RAS+NF1) by KIT nonsilent mutant status; use Fisher exact test, report odds ratio and counts. IF FOUND: if expected counts <5 use Fisher only; a higher fraction with p<0.05 supports enrichment; similar or lower fraction contradicts. SOURCE: domain knowledge (search unavailable).

label: Unmatched tumours germline
text: PITFALL: Primary tumours are 'Unmatched' (no normal) while xenografts are 'Matched' (SOMATIC_STATUS column), so germline SNPs survive in tumour calls and inflate apparent 'mutations lost in xenograft'. CHECK: tabulate SOMATIC_STATUS by SAMPLE_CLASS; check how many T-only variants have dbSNP IDs or sit at ~50% (if any allele info). IF FOUND: remove likely germline/dbSNP variants before calling a mutation lost; prefer CNA-based or shared-variant evidence. SOURCE: domain knowledge (search tool failed)

label: Gene symbol aliases and multiple-symbol columns
text: PITFALL: The variant may be annotated under Hugo_Symbol of a neighbouring gene, or with Entrez_Gene_Id 0 (as in this file), or only in all_effects. An exact Hugo_Symbol=='NFKBIE' filter can miss it. CHECK: search NFKBIE case-insensitively in Hugo_Symbol, SYMBOL and all_effects, and also search by coordinate window. IF FOUND: include those rows. SOURCE: https://www.ensembl.org/info/docs/tools/vep/vep_formats.html (not retrieved)

label: ID joins and patient level
text: PITFALL: Samples in the clinical table may have no rows in the MAF, and IDs may differ between tables or a patient may have several samples. That distorts denominators and patient-level counts. CHECK: join Tumor_Sample_Barcode to SAMPLE_ID/PATIENT_ID and list unmatched IDs and patients with more than one sample. IF FOUND: count at patient level, and treat samples with no MAF rows as having no detected mutation rather than dropping them silently. SOURCE: cBioPortal file-format conventions (web search unavailable).

label: KIT in other subtypes
text: PITFALL: A subtype-defining gene (BRAF/NRAS/NF1) can co-occur with KIT; if Triple-WT is defined as lacking BRAF/RAS/NF1, KIT mutations in other groups are real but may be passengers. CHECK: list KIT mutant samples with their subtype and protein change. IF FOUND: interpret enrichment based on driver KIT mutations; note co-occurring cases. SOURCE: domain knowledge (search unavailable).

label: Purity confounds CNA
text: PITFALL: Mouse stromal cells in xenografts and human stroma in primaries change tumour purity, which shifts log2 CNA amplitudes and can create apparent copy-number 'changes' that are really purity differences. CHECK: compare whether segment differences between T and X are shifts in amplitude across the whole genome (purity) versus discrete new/lost breakpoints or arm-level events. IF FOUND: treat only discrete gains/losses or new breakpoints as clonal changes; rescale by estimated purity before comparing amplitudes. SOURCE: domain knowledge (search tool failed); e.g. ABSOLUTE https://www.nature.com/articles/nbt.2203

label: No primary/met label
text: PITFALL: The hypothesis says primary AND metastatic tumours, but data_clinical_sample.txt has no primary/metastasis column. CHECK: look for any column or ID note that separates primary from metastatic origin. IF FOUND (no such field): judge clonal selection at engraftment over all patients, and say in the reasoning that primary vs metastatic cannot be separated; do not choose Not verifiable only for that reason if engraftment selection itself is evaluable. SOURCE: domain knowledge (search tool failed)

label: Define selection properly
text: PITFALL: Clonal selection means a shift in the clonal makeup (some clones expand, others are lost), not simply that a mutation is missing; sequencing depth differences and passage noise also cause drop-out. CHECK: count, per patient, how many T vs X0/X1 differences are systematic (many co-occurring events, CNA segments) versus a few isolated low-coverage variants; check whether the same changes recur across sibling xenografts (A/B/C). IF FOUND: count consistent multi-event shifts in many patients as selection; isolated single-variant differences are weak evidence. SOURCE: domain knowledge (search tool failed)

label: SV table lacks breakpoints for chromoplexy
text: PITFALL: Chromoplexy is defined from WGS rearrangement breakpoint junctions (chains of balanced translocations/deletions whose breakpoints join each other, e.g. ChainFinder); without breakpoint coordinates and junction partners it cannot be inferred. CHECK: Inspect data_sv.txt: here it has 27 data rows, columns Sample_Id, Site1/Site2_Hugo_Symbol, RNA_Support, SV_Status, Center, Event_Info - no chromosome/position columns, and every row is Event_Info=Fusion (26 ERG-ERG, 1 ETV1, 1 BRAF). IF FOUND: The per-junction data needed to model rearrangement genesis or detect interdependent chains is absent; weigh 'Not verifiable' rather than forcing True/False from proxies. SOURCE: background knowledge only (research tool returned HTTP 403 on all calls).

label: Use paired pre/post samples
text: PITFALL: The claim concerns within-patient selection over time, but most samples are unpaired (about 197 PRE-TX primaries vs about 90 POST-TX samples), so pooled pre-vs-post ERBB2 rates confound selection with which patients got rebiopsied. CHECK: count patients with both a PRE-TX and a POST-TX sample (IMPACT_PRE_POST) that both have ERBB2 copy-number data, and tabulate ERBB2 status in each pair. IF FOUND: base the main inference on paired patients (amplified pre -> non-amplified post = loss/selection); use unpaired comparisons only as support. SOURCE: domain knowledge; research tool unavailable (HTTP 403).

label: ETS fusion is not chromoplexy
text: PITFALL: Treating ETS fusions (ERG/ETV1 rows in data_sv.txt, ETS_FUSION_SEQ / ERG_FISH_RESULT in the sample table) as evidence of chromoplexy; TMPRSS2-ERG can arise from a simple 21q interstitial deletion or a single translocation. CHECK: Check whether any column records fusion mechanism, partner chains, or breakpoint coordinates. IF FOUND: Fusion frequency alone neither supports nor refutes chromoplexy; do not equate fusion presence with chromoplexy. SOURCE: background knowledge only (research tool returned HTTP 403 on all calls).

label: Sample ID harmonisation
text: PITFALL: Sample IDs differ between tables (clinical uses e.g. s_YJ_her_003_P1, data_cna.txt columns use e.g. YJ-her-004-P), so naive joins silently drop the paired research samples that matter most. CHECK: compare SAMPLE_ID sets across clinical, data_cna.txt, the seg file and the panel matrix; count unmatched IDs. IF FOUND: harmonise IDs (underscore/hyphen, s_ prefix, case) before any analysis and report how many pairs survive. SOURCE: domain knowledge; research tool unavailable.

label: CN segments cannot show chromoplexy
text: PITFALL: Using segmented copy number (data_cna_hg19.seg, data_cna.txt, data_log2_cna.txt) as a proxy; chromoplexy is largely copy-neutral with small junction deletions, so CN cannot reveal which breaks are interconnected. CHECK: The seg file has only ID, chrom, loc.start, loc.end, num.mark, seg.mean - no junction partners. IF FOUND: CN breakpoint/deletion counts describe instability but cannot establish interdependent chains; state the limitation and do not count it as support. SOURCE: background knowledge only (research tool returned HTTP 403 on all calls).

label: Purity mimics ERBB2 loss
text: PITFALL: Low tumour purity in a post-treatment biopsy makes ERBB2 look non-amplified, mimicking loss of the amplified clone. CHECK: for every apparent loss, look at the continuous ERBB2 log ratio (HER2_IMPACT_LR, seg.mean at chr17 ~39.68-39.73 Mb hg19) and at sample FGA / other arm-level CNAs; a flat genome with low FGA suggests low purity. IF FOUND: flag or exclude low-purity samples; count a loss as real only if other clonal CNAs are still visible while ERBB2 is neutral. SOURCE: domain knowledge; research tool unavailable.

label: chromoplexy vs chromothripsis
text: PITFALL: Confusing chromoplexy with chromothripsis: chromothripsis = many clustered breaks on one/few chromosomes with oscillating 2-state CN; chromoplexy = fewer breaks across multiple chromosomes in chained, often balanced junctions. CHECK: If 'complex events' are inferred from CN oscillation on a single chromosome, that is a chromothripsis signature. IF FOUND: Do not report such patterns as support for chromoplexy. SOURCE: background knowledge only (research tool returned HTTP 403 on all calls).

label: Discrete vs continuous ERBB2 calls
text: PITFALL: Discrete CNA calls (data_cna.txt 2 = amp) and the HER2_IMPACT field use thresholds; a drop from 2 to 1 can be a modest log-ratio change, not loss of the amplified subclone. text: If VTE and anticoagulation data do exist, a naive comparison of VTE rates between treated and untreated patients is biased in three ways. Confounding by indication: higher-risk patients are the ones who get anticoagulated. Immortal time bias. Death as a competing risk. To handle this, use landmark or time-varying exposure, competing-risk cumulative incidence or Fine-Gray models, and test the anticoagulation x ctDNA interaction directly instead of comparing p-values between subgroups. The hypothesis is a negative claim: a non-significant result in a small subgroup does not by itself show there is no benefit.

text: NFKBIE (chr6p21.1, roughly chr6:44.225-44.233 Mb in GRCh37; check NCBI_Build) is on the minus strand. Its promoter/TSS is therefore at the HIGHER-coordinate end of the gene, not below the start coordinate. Look for promoter variants by coordinate window (about 2 kb around the TSS of canonical transcript ENST00000275015) as well as by gene name. Promoter variants may be annotated to a neighbouring gene's Hugo_Symbol, carry Entrez_Gene_Id 0, or name NFKBIE only in SYMBOL/all_effects, so search those columns case-insensitively. Note whether hits recur at the same position and whether they are UV-type C>T/CC>TT changes.

Compare Harrell's C-index (with a bootstrap CI for the difference) and AIC, and run a likelihood-ratio test of adding PROGNOSTIC_MODEL to IPI. In the joint model, check whether the genetic model stays independently prognostic after IPI adjustment, and check proportional hazards (Schoenfeld residuals / cox.zph). reason: The hypothesis turns on what 'significantly mutated' means. Without a background model, teams may judge it from raw percentages alone.
text: 'Significantly mutated pathway' is a statistical claim: the pathway is mutated more than expected under a background mutation rate that accounts for gene coding length and per-sample mutation burden. Raw frequency is not significance, and large genes (e.g. ERBB2-4, PIK3C2G) dominate pathway counts. Count samples with a nonsynonymous hit in the pathway gene set, compare that with an expectation from a permutation or binomial model (coding length x cohort nonsynonymous rate; TMB_NONSYNONYMOUS is available), and base the call on the pathway-level p/q-value. Report the percentage of samples affected as well.

reason: Different gene sets can flip the conclusion, so the teams need a defensible primary definition and a sensitivity check.
text: The gene set definition drives the result. Run the test with a core ERBB-PI3K set (EGFR, ERBB2, ERBB3, ERBB4, PIK3CA, PIK3CB, PIK3R1, PTEN, AKT1-3, MTOR, TSC1/2) and with an extended set (e.g. KEGG hsa04012, which is much larger and can become 'significant' because of its size). List which genes carry hits. If the two disagree, report the core-set result as primary and state the sensitivity.

reason: This is the main reasoning trap in a negative hypothesis: treating absence of evidence or low power as support.
text: The hypothesis is a negative claim ('not significantly mutated'). The cohort is small (about 56 sequenced samples) and has a low mutation burden, so failing to reach significance is weak evidence. Count samples with nonsynonymous hits in the core genes, and use the Hotspot column to look for recurrent or hotspot hits (e.g. PIK3CA E542K/E545K/H1047R). Judge the label on the enrichment test and the fraction of samples hit. Do not choose 'True' just because no formal significance has been shown, and say how statistical power affected your call.

reason: Counting non-coding or silent variants inflates the pathway alteration rate.
text: Count only nonsynonymous variant classes as pathway mutations: Missense, Nonsense, Frame_Shift, In_Frame indels, Splice_Site, Translation_Start_Site and Nonstop. QUESTION: In melanoma genomic subtyping, is the 'triple wild-type' class defined only by the absence of BRAF, RAS and NF1 mutations, and are KIT-mutant tumours that also carry one of those mutations assigned to the other class? From background knowledge, the optimism in an apparent C-index depends on the number of events per candidate parameter and on any data-driven selection. For a prespecified model with few parameters and >=10-20 events per parameter, it is usually small, about 0.01-0.03. With variable or cutpoint selection, or few events, it is often 0.05-0.10 or more. Standard corrections follow Harrell/Efron: in the bootstrap, refit the whole modelling process, including selection, on each of 200+ resamples and subtract the mean optimism (bootstrap C minus C on the original data) from the apparent C. question: FINDING FROM THE LAB'S LIBRARY, asked for by the director. QUESTION: Which prognostic tools are considered current established methods for risk stratification in diffuse large B-cell lymphoma treated with R-CHOP (e.g. IPI, R-IPI, NCCN-IPI, cell of origin, double-hit FISH)? How is each defined? ANSWER: NOT WEB-VERIFIED (gateway HTTP 403); background knowledge only. IPI (1993) scores 1 point each for age >60, stage III/IV, elevated LDH, ECOG >=2 and >1 extranodal site; groups are 0-1 low, 2 low-intermediate, 3 high-intermediate, 4-5 high. R-IPI (Sehn 2007) regroups the same factors as 0 very good, 1-2 good, 3-5 poor. NCCN-IPI (Zhou 2014) scores 0-8: age 41-60=1, 61-75=2, >75=3; LDH ratio >1-3=1, >3=2; stage III/IV=1; ECOG>=2=1; extranodal disease in marrow, CNS, liver/GI or lung=1. Its groups are 0-1, 2-3, 4-5 and >=6, and it discriminates better than IPI in the rituximab era. Cell of origin (GCB vs ABC/non-GCB) comes from gene expression profiling or IHC algorithms (e.g. Hans); ABC has the worse outcome. Double-hit or triple-hit status is MYC rearrangement plus BCL2 and/or BCL6 rearrangement by FISH (WHO HGBL-DH/TH) and has a poor prognosis. Other tools are MYC/BCL2 double expression by IHC and CNS-IPI for CNS relapse. IPI (or a variant) is the universal clinical comparator; COO and double-hit status are the main established biological stratifiers. HOW SURE: medium. SOURCES: none given.

The observed ratio is about (p*C + 2(1-p)) / (p*ploidy + 2(1-p)), so at purity 0.3 a one-copy loss is about -0.23 and a one-copy gain about +0.20, close to typical calling thresholds. Standard practice is to estimate purity (ABSOLUTE, ASCAT, FACETS, Sequenza, PureCN, or roughly 2x the median VAF of clonal heterozygous somatic SNVs in copy-neutral regions) and then rescale log2 ratios before thresholding and computing FGA (e.g. CNVkit call --purity). VAF-based purity needs enough somatic mutations to be reliable, so for a low-TMB lesion it is weak. Purity is therefore a real and partly correctable confound, but with sparse mutations it stays a caveat rather than a dependable adjustment. HOW SURE: low. SOURCES: none given.

ANSWER: NOT WEB-VERIFIED: the research gateway returned HTTP 403 on all 4 calls, so this comes from domain knowledge only. Normal-cell contamination pulls log2 ratios toward 0. The observed ratio is about (p*C + 2(1-p)) / (p*ploidy + 2(1-p)), so at purity 0.3 a one-copy loss is about -0.23 and a one-copy gain about +0.20, close to typical calling thresholds. Standard practice is to estimate purity (ABSOLUTE, ASCAT, FACETS, Sequenza, PureCN, or roughly 2x the median VAF of clonal heterozygous somatic SNVs in copy-neutral regions) and then rescale log2 ratios before thresholding and computing FGA (e.g. CNVkit call --purity). VAF-based purity needs enough somatic mutations to be reliable, so for a low-TMB lesion it is weak. Purity is therefore a real and partly correctable confound, but with sparse mutations it stays a caveat rather than a dependable adjustment. HOW SURE: low. SOURCES: none given.

QUESTION: In cancer genomics, when a paper reports a lesion as having a 'high number of copy number alterations', is that usually a count of discrete segments or breakpoints, or a genome-fraction metric? Which segment-mean thresholds are conventional for calling gains and losses from exome-derived segmentation? ANSWER: NOT WEB-VERIFIED: the gateway returned HTTP 403, so this comes from domain knowledge only. Papers use both readings: a count of altered segments or events, or a genome fraction (FGA or percent genome altered). Which one is meant has to be checked case by case, so robust analyses report both. Conventional log2 thresholds: cBioPortal FGA uses |seg.mean| > 0.2; CNVkit call defaults are -1.1/-0.25/+0.2/+0.7; GATK CallCopyRatioSegments treats copy ratio 0.9-1.1 (log2 about -0.15/+0.14) as neutral; GISTIC uses a noise threshold of 0.1; ±0.3 is common for noisy exome data. The ranking should be checked to hold across thresholds of 0.1-0.3. HOW SURE: low. SOURCES: none given.

question: FINDING FROM THE LAB'S LIBRARY, asked for by the director. QUESTION: In paired pre/post-treatment tumour sequencing studies, what evidence is usually required to call loss of an oncogene amplification 'selection of a pre-existing subclone' rather than spatial heterogeneity, low purity or a different primary tumour? ANSWER: No formal standard exists. Usual evidence: (a) shared truncal mutations/clonal CNAs between the pre- and post-treatment samples, which rules out a different primary or a sample swap; (b) adequate post-treatment purity, with other clonal CNAs still present while ERBB2 is neutral, which rules out low purity; (c) pre-treatment evidence of ERBB2 heterogeneity (heterogeneous FISH/IHC, multi-region discordance, or a subclonal amplification/non-amplified subclone found by cancer cell fraction analysis); (d) comparison of the same or matched sites, or with untreated site-discordance rates, which addresses spatial heterogeneity. Without (c), loss after treatment fits selection but does not prove it. Not web-verified (gateway down). HOW SURE: medium. SOURCES: none given.

text: FINDING: UNVERIFIED (web search gateway returned HTTP 403 on all 4 calls; answer from background knowledge). For a multi-gene enrichment claim, the usual genomics practice (e.g. MSK-IMPACT sidedness papers) is a per-gene Fisher test with FDR (BH) correction across genes; a composite 'any of the genes' test answers a different, weaker question. With a mix of significant and non-significant genes, a conjunctive claim ('enriched in KRAS, BRAF, PIK3CA, AKT1, RNF43 and SMAD4') is only partly supported. Non-significant genes with the same direction count as weak or underpowered support, not contradiction. A significant opposite-direction gene contradicts that part. question: FINDING FROM THE LAB'S LIBRARY, asked for by the director. QUESTION: How do standard significantly-mutated-pathway methods (e.g. PathScan, MutSigCV-style pathway aggregation, or permutation of gene labels) define the background mutation rate? Do they correct for multiple testing across pathways when calling one pathway 'significantly mutated'? ANSWER: NOT SETTLED BY WEB: the research gateway returned HTTP 502/403 on all 4 calls, so no page was read. From domain knowledge only: PathScan builds a per-gene background from coding length x background mutation rate and combines samples with a convolution/Fisher test, which is close to the teams' length x rate Poisson model. MutSigCV uses covariate-adjusted per-gene rates. Papers that screen many pathways typically report FDR/q-values, but a single prespecified pathway is often reported at nominal p<0.05. An uncorrected p near 0.05 is borderline and not robust. HOW SURE: low. SOURCES: none given.

question: FINDING FROM THE LAB'S LIBRARY, asked for by the director. QUESTION: In common pathway annotations, is the 'ERBB-PI3K' pathway usually defined to include RAS genes (KRAS, NRAS, HRAS), or only receptors, PI3K subunits, PTEN, AKT, mTOR and TSC? ANSWER: NOT SETTLED BY WEB (gateway failed). From domain knowledge only: KEGG ErbB (hsa04012) and KEGG PI3K-Akt (hsa04151) include KRAS, NRAS and HRAS. Curated cancer-genomics sets (TCGA Sanchez-Vega 2018) place RAS in a separate RTK-RAS pathway and keep PI3K/PTEN/AKT/mTOR/TSC separate. 'ERBB-PI3K' in NPC papers is usually receptors plus PI3K-AKT-mTOR genes, but whether RAS is included is uncertain. Report the result both with and without RAS. HOW SURE: low. SOURCES: none given.

question: FINDING FROM THE LAB'S LIBRARY, asked for by the director. QUESTION: How is TMB (nonsynonymous mutations per Mb) conventionally computed for whole-exome data: what denominator is typically used, and how does that compare with the effective callable exome used in background-rate models? ANSWER: NOT SETTLED BY WEB (gateway failed). From domain knowledge only: the denominator is the callable/target coding territory, commonly about 30-38 Mb (about 38 Mb in TCGA MC3-based work, 30 Mb in many tools). The effective per-sample callable exome is often about 25-33 Mb. If the background rate is estimated as observed count/target and the expectation is rate x pathway coding length, the target size largely cancels (only pathway length/target matters), so the borderline p-value should be fairly insensitive to the 30 Mb assumption. It shifts only if TMB is taken as given and then multiplied back with a different denominator. HOW SURE: low. SOURCES: none given.

The data never show FN acquiring fewer. The 'no common mutations' half is weak because the TP53 recurrence rests on 2 patients, one with a 10%-purity baseline. The label stays False.

text: REPLY Q4 sample count/LOO: Later samples per patient are identical by group (FN 9x1 + 1x2; FP 9x1 + 1x2). OS_MONTHS: FN median 32.2, FP median 19.2 (means 25.9 vs 29.5). Per later sample, FN 6.7 vs FP 1.3, p=0.0039. Leaving out any one patient gives MWU p between 0.0034 and 0.0144 (per-sample version max 0.0068). text: REPLY library findings: Purity finding checked; it applies to 4 FN pairs where baseline purity was lower, but excluding low-purity samples keeps FN>FP (p=0.026). Collapsing amplicons was checked; FN>FP holds (4.0 vs 1.4, p=0.0099). Zero-alt-read genotyping of the baseline is not possible with these files (no fill-out). Neither finding reverses the direction.

text: REPLY (seg/shallow CNA question): All new deep CNAs had gene-level 0 in the earliest sample. But the seg file shows two big clusters already had a pre-existing shift: P-0013120 16q at -0.54 in a 30%-purity first sample, and P-0048073 17q at +0.80. Those 11 + 14 gene calls are threshold effects. After collapsing genes by chromosome arm, FN median is 3.5 (0-7) vs FP 1.5 (0-3), p=0.024. Dropping the 16q/17q events gives FN median 3 vs FP 1.5. Counting only mutations+SVs (no CNA at all) gives FN 1.5 vs FP 0.5. FN still acquires more; method not changed in direction.

text: REPLY (panel/VAF question): Restricting to the 541 genes non-NA in every sample (the shared IMPACT410/468/505 content) gives FN median 5.5 (0-18) vs FP 1.5 (0-3), p=0.016. No new mutation had VAF <5%; the lowest were KMT2A 0.061 and PTPRD 0.067. Counts are essentially unchanged.

text: REPLY (mutation-only commonality question): Using point mutations only, TP53 is newly acquired in 2 FN patients: P-0051132 (VAF 0.50) and P-0073133 (VAF 0.89). text: REPLY Q1 (germline/artefact/benign): none of the 9 ERBB-PI3K pathway calls is FILTER=common_variant; all have ExAC_AF missing or <=1.7e-5 and no GMAF; the MAF has no t/n read counts so VAF vs cellularity cannot be computed. MTOR A1778S and NRG1 R5H are predicted benign, and NRAS Q61R is tool-benign but a known hotspot. Dropping benign calls only from the pathway count makes it non-significant (p 0.08-0.17). Applying the same SIFT-tolerated+PolyPhen-benign filter to the background too keeps it significant (full 7 vs 2.69 expected, p=0.020; core 6 vs 2.54, p=0.045). Method unchanged.

text: REPLY Q2 (core genes, samples, permutation): full set incl RAS gives 9 mutations vs 3.67 expected (Poisson p=0.013), 7 samples vs 3.3 expected (permutation keeping each sample's count, p=0.034), mutation permutation p=0.012. Core receptor/PI3K/AKT/mTOR set without RAS/BRAF gives 7 vs 3.47 (p=0.063), samples p=0.079, and p=0.021 excluding hypermutator NPC15F. The exome denominator matters: core p is 0.096 at 27 Mb and 0.022 at 38 Mb. Significance depends on including RAS, so confidence is lower but the label is unchanged.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY Q3 (random gene sets/other pathways): length-matched (+-15%) random gene sets, with the genome padded with unmutated genes up to 30.8 Mb, give a mean of 3.8 for the full ERBB-PI3K set vs 9 observed (p=0.017); the core set gives 3.65 vs 7 (p=0.082). Across 11 pathways ERBB-PI3K full has BH q=0.026 but Bonferroni 0.14; chromatin, TP53, RTK-RAS and Notch are stronger. Enrichment is modest and real under FDR, not under Bonferroni. Label False is kept, confidence lowered.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY Q1 (VAF/functional): t_alt_count, t_ref_count and n_alt_count are '.' for all 1575 rows (t_depth=0), so VAF and normal-read checks cannot be done. SIFT/PolyPhen: MTOR A1778S is tolerated/benign (MA low). ERBB2 I767M, ERBB3 K329R/E919K, TSC1 R22W and PIK3CA E545K are deleterious/damaging. NRAS Q61R is called tolerated/benign although it is a known hotspot, so the predictors are unreliable. Restricting observed and expected counts to functional mutations (73.8% of all NS) gives 5 obs vs 1.87 exp, p=0.042 (4/56 samples). Dropping only MTOR with an unrestricted background gives p=0.11, which is not a consistent comparison. Method not changed.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY Q2 (empirical background): CDS lengths for 1333 mutated genes came from the CDS_position denominators. Within length bins of +/-25%, only ERBB3 (2 hits) stands out from other mutated genes, and 8.9% of length-matched mutated genes also have >=2 hits. 116 genes have >=2 mutations against 98 expected under uniform Poisson, so the data are modestly overdispersed and the Poisson core-set p=0.045 is somewhat anti-conservative. The per-sample permutation p was 0.07. The core-set result without RAS is borderline and not robustly <0.05. Label not changed, but confidence lowered.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY Q3 (multiple pathways): The same length x cohort-rate Poisson test was run on 13 Sanchez-Vega-style pathways (lengths from the MAF CDS_position, 1700 bp default for unmutated genes without a known length). 6/13 have p<0.05: TP53, chromatin, RTK-RAS, NF-kB, Notch, ERBB-PI3K core. ERBB-PI3K core has BH q=0.097 (<0.1, barely), and RTK-RAS (incl. ERBB2/3, KRAS, NRAS) has q=0.003. The narrow PI3K-only set (no receptors) has p=0.38. Many cancer pathways come out nominally significant, so the uniform background is lenient. ERBB-PI3K still survives BH at 0.1, so the label is kept, with weak evidence.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY (library findings): The claim that the exome target size cancels is wrong for this test. Expected pathway count = total NS x pathway length / T, so T matters. With T=30 Mb, which is below the ~33 Mb CCDS exome, the expected count is larger, so the test is conservative; a 38 Mb target would lower p. Following the RAS finding, the result is reported with and without RAS: core p~0.045 (q=0.097 across 13 pathways), core+RAS p=0.007-0.016. Label unchanged (False).
